# Media Card

An image card with a glass caption over a soft scrim. With `href`, the whole card is one link.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Layout · Status: beta
- Import: `import { MediaCard } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/media-card

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` (required) | `string` |  | Image URL. Loaded lazily. |
| `alt` (required) | `string` |  | Image description. Pass '' when the image is decorative. |
| `ratio` | `'16/9' \| '4/3' \| '1/1' \| '3/4'` | `'16/9'` | Aspect ratio of the image box. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | Caption title, rendered as an h3. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Caption text under the title. |
| `eyebrow` | `ReactNode` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `href` | `string` |  | Makes the whole card one link, stretched from the title (so it needs `title`). Adds the hover lift and image zoom. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Actions under the caption. They stay clickable above the stretched link. |

## Example: With link

```tsx
<MediaCard
  src="/covers/lisbon.jpg"
  alt=""
  eyebrow="Guide"
  title="A weekend in Lisbon"
  description="Where to eat, walk and stay."
  href="/guides/lisbon"
/>
```

## Example: Without link, with actions

```tsx
<MediaCard src="/covers/q3.jpg" alt="" title="Q3 brand shoot" description="48 photos">
  <Button size="sm" variant="tonal">Open</Button>
  <Button size="sm" variant="text">Share</Button>
</MediaCard>
```

## Example: Ratios

```tsx
<MediaCard ratio="16/9" src={src} alt="" title="16/9" />
<MediaCard ratio="4/3" src={src} alt="" title="4/3" />
<MediaCard ratio="1/1" src={src} alt="" title="1/1" />
<MediaCard ratio="3/4" src={src} alt="" title="3/4" />
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: link (when `href` is set), heading level 3 (title)
- `Tab`: Focuses the link (the card shows the focus ring), then any actions.
- `Enter`: Follows the link.
- With `href`, the link’s name is the title only, not the whole caption.
- Most card images repeat the title, so `alt=""` is usually right.

Related: [card](card.md)


---

# Message Bubble

One message in a conversation. User messages sit in a bubble at the end; assistant replies run full width. MessageActions adds copy, feedback and regenerate.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: AI · Status: beta
- Import: `import { MessageBubble } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/message-bubble

## When to use

- Each turn in a chat or assistant thread, inside Conversation.
- MessageActions under assistant replies the user may want to copy, rate or retry.

## When not to use

- Comment threads and activity logs: use ActivityFeed or NotificationItem.
- Model output as HTML: render text or React elements as children, never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` (required) | `'user' \| 'assistant' \| 'system'` |  | Who sent it. Sets layout and the default accessible name. |
| `avatar` | `ReactNode` |  | Assistant only: shown at the inline start. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the message. Defaults to "You said" or "Assistant said". |
| `status` | `'sending' \| 'error'` |  | `sending` sets `aria-busy`; `error` shows "Failed to send". |
| `onRetry` | `() => void` |  | With `status="error"`, adds a Retry button. |
| `messages` | `Partial<MessageStrings>` |  | Local string overrides. |
| `MessageActions text` | `string` |  | Text Copy puts on the clipboard. |
| `MessageActions copy` | `boolean` | `true` | Set false to hide Copy. |
| `MessageActions feedback / defaultFeedback / onFeedback` | `'up' \| 'down' \| null` |  | Thumbs up/down appear when `onFeedback` is set. Pressing the active one clears it. |
| `MessageActions onRegenerate` | `() => void` |  | Shows Regenerate when set. |

## Example: Conversation

Hover or focus the assistant reply to show its actions.

```tsx
<MessageBubble from="user">How do I cancel my subscription?</MessageBubble>
<MessageBubble from="assistant" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback={<Sparkles />} />}>
  <p>Open Settings, then Billing, and choose Cancel plan. You keep access until the end of the billing period.</p>
  <MessageActions
    text="Open Settings, then Billing, and choose Cancel plan."
    onFeedback={(value) => logFeedback(value)}
    onRegenerate={() => regenerate()}
  />
</MessageBubble>
<MessageBubble from="system">Conversation moved to Billing support</MessageBubble>
```

## Example: Failed to send

```tsx
<MessageBubble from="user" status="error" onRetry={() => resend()}>
  Can I get a refund for last month?
</MessageBubble>
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: article (each message), alert (send error), button (actions)
- `Tab`: Moves through the action buttons; focusing one reveals the row.
- `Space / Enter`: Activates an action. Feedback buttons toggle.
- Each message is an `article` named "You said" or "Assistant said", so users can jump between messages.
- Feedback buttons expose `aria-pressed`. Copy announces "Copied" through a status region.
- The action row is only visually hidden until hover; it stays in the tab order and accessibility tree.

Related: [streaming-text](streaming-text.md), [conversation](conversation.md), [citation](citation.md)


---

# Money Input

An amount field: locale-aware parsing as you type, grouped on blur, the currency symbol leading.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Form & Input · Status: beta
- Import: `import { MoneyInput } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/money-input

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` (required) | `string` |  | ISO 4217 code, e.g. "EUR". |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale for separators. Defaults to the user's. |
| `value / defaultValue` | `number \| null` |  | The amount, or null when empty. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number \| null) => void` |  | Parsed amount, rounded to the minor unit, as the person types. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<MoneyInput aria-label="Amount to send" currency="USD" defaultValue={1250} onValueChange={setAmount} />
```

## Example: German separators

```tsx
<MoneyInput aria-label="Betrag" currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" defaultValue={1234.5} />
```

Related: [amount](amount.md), [number-input](number-input.md), [input](input.md)

# Collapse

Expands and collapses content along the block axis.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Motion · Status: stable
- Import: `import { MotionCollapse } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/motion-collapse

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in` (required) | `boolean` |  | When true, expands the content to its natural height. When false, collapses it to zero height. |
| `duration` | `'instant' \| 'fast' \| 'normal' \| 'slow' \| 'slower'` | `'normal'` | Controls the animation speed using the design token scale. |
| `easing` | `'linear' \| 'in' \| 'out' \| 'in-out' \| 'out-expo' \| 'spring'` | `'out'` | Easing curve applied to the animation. |
| `unmountOnExit` | `boolean` | `false` | Removes the element from the DOM after the collapse animation completes. |
| `as` | `React.ElementType` | `'div'` | The HTML element or component to render as the wrapper. |
| `children` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content to expand and collapse. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Collapse in={true}>
  <div style={{ padding: '16px', background: 'var(--color-bg-subtle)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)' }}>
    Collapsed content
  </div>
</Collapse>
```

## Example: Toggle

```tsx
function CollapseToggle() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '8px' }}>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}>
        {open ? 'Collapse' : 'Expand'}
      </Button>
      <Collapse in={open} unmountOnExit>
        <div
          style={{
            padding: '16px',
            background: 'var(--color-bg-subtle)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)',
            color: 'var(--color-text-secondary)',
            fontSize: '0.875rem',
          }}
        >
          This section smoothly expands and collapses along the vertical axis.
          It preserves the natural document flow by animating the block size.
        </div>
      </Collapse>
    </div>
  );
}
```


---

# Fade

Animates opacity between 0 and 1 based on the `in` prop.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Motion · Status: stable
- Import: `import { MotionFade } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/motion-fade

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in` (required) | `boolean` |  | When true, fades content in. When false, fades it out. |
| `duration` | `'instant' \| 'fast' \| 'normal' \| 'slow' \| 'slower'` | `'normal'` | Controls the animation speed using the design token scale. |
| `easing` | `'linear' \| 'in' \| 'out' \| 'in-out' \| 'out-expo' \| 'spring'` | `'out'` | Easing curve applied to the animation. |
| `unmountOnExit` | `boolean` | `false` | Removes the element from the DOM after the exit animation completes. |
| `as` | `React.ElementType` | `'div'` | The HTML element or component to render as the wrapper. |
| `children` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content to animate. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Fade in={true}>
  <Card>Faded in content</Card>
</Fade>
```

## Example: Toggle

```tsx
function FadeToggle() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = React.useState(true);
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '16px' }}>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setVisible((v) => !v)}>
        {visible ? 'Fade out' : 'Fade in'}
      </Button>
      <Fade in={visible} duration="normal" easing="out" unmountOnExit>
        <Card style={{ padding: '16px' }}>
          This content fades in and out. Toggle the button to animate it.
        </Card>
      </Fade>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example: Slow with spring easing

```tsx
function SlowFade() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = React.useState(true);
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '16px' }}>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setVisible((v) => !v)}>Toggle</Button>
      <Fade in={visible} duration="slow" easing="spring">
        <div style={{ padding: '16px', background: 'var(--color-bg-subtle)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)' }}>
          Slow spring fade animation.
        </div>
      </Fade>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Scale

Scales content in/out from its center.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Motion · Status: stable
- Import: `import { MotionScale } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/motion-scale

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in` (required) | `boolean` |  | When true, scales content in from 0 to 1. When false, scales it back down to 0. |
| `duration` | `'instant' \| 'fast' \| 'normal' \| 'slow' \| 'slower'` | `'normal'` | Controls the animation speed using the design token scale. |
| `easing` | `'linear' \| 'in' \| 'out' \| 'in-out' \| 'out-expo' \| 'spring'` | `'out'` | Easing curve applied to the animation. |
| `unmountOnExit` | `boolean` | `false` | Removes the element from the DOM after the exit animation completes. |
| `as` | `React.ElementType` | `'div'` | The HTML element or component to render as the wrapper. |
| `children` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content to animate. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Scale in={true}>
  <Card>Scaled content</Card>
</Scale>
```

## Example: Toggle

```tsx
function ScaleToggle() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = React.useState(true);
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '16px' }}>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setVisible((v) => !v)}>
        {visible ? 'Scale out' : 'Scale in'}
      </Button>
      <Scale in={visible} duration="fast" easing="spring" unmountOnExit>
        <div
          style={{
            padding: '24px',
            background: 'var(--color-bg-subtle)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)',
            textAlign: 'center',
            color: 'var(--color-text-secondary)',
          }}
        >
          Pop!
        </div>
      </Scale>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Slide

Slides content in from a direction based on the `in` prop.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Motion · Status: stable
- Import: `import { MotionSlide } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/motion-slide

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in` (required) | `boolean` |  | When true, slides content in. When false, slides it out. |
| `direction` | `'up' \| 'down' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `'up'` | The direction from which the content slides in. |
| `duration` | `'instant' \| 'fast' \| 'normal' \| 'slow' \| 'slower'` | `'normal'` | Controls the animation speed using the design token scale. |
| `easing` | `'linear' \| 'in' \| 'out' \| 'in-out' \| 'out-expo' \| 'spring'` | `'out'` | Easing curve applied to the animation. |
| `unmountOnExit` | `boolean` | `false` | Removes the element from the DOM after the exit animation completes. |
| `as` | `React.ElementType` | `'div'` | The HTML element or component to render as the wrapper. |
| `children` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content to animate. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Slide in={true} direction="up">
  <Card>Slid in from bottom</Card>
</Slide>
```

## Example: Directions

```tsx
function SlideDirections() {
  const [visible, setVisible] = React.useState(true);
  const [direction, setDirection] = React.useState('up');
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '16px' }}>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '8px', flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
        {['up', 'down', 'left', 'right'].map((dir) => (
          <Button
            key={dir}
            variant={direction === dir ? 'primary' : 'outline'}
            size="sm"
            onClick={() => { setDirection(dir); setVisible(true); }}
          >
            {dir}
          </Button>
        ))}
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setVisible((v) => !v)}>
          Toggle
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Slide in={visible} direction={direction} unmountOnExit>
        <div style={{ padding: '16px', background: 'var(--color-bg-subtle)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)' }}>
          Sliding in from {direction}.
        </div>
      </Slide>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Navigation Rail

Navigation for medium-width windows: icons over labels, with an active pill behind the icon.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Navigation · Status: beta
- Import: `import { NavigationRail } from '@nexub/react';`

| `Root aria-label` | `string` | `'Main'` | Name of the nav landmark. |
| `Item icon / label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Icon in the indicator pill; label below. |
| `Item active` | `boolean` |  | Marks the current page (aria-current="page"). |

## Example: Default


# Number Ticker

A number whose digits roll to new values on the spatial spring. The first render never animates.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Data Display · Status: beta
- Import: `import { NumberTicker } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/number-ticker

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `number \| string \| NumberTickerPart[]` |  | A number (formatted with `format` and `locale`), an already-formatted string, or styled parts. |
| `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | Formatting for a number `value`. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | BCP 47 locale. Defaults to the user's. |
| `aria-live` | `'off' \| 'polite'` | `'off'` | Announce changes to screen readers. Use `polite` only for values the user is waiting on. |

## Example: Formatted number

Each digit is a 0–9 strip; separators and symbols stay still.

```tsx
const [n, setN] = React.useState(12480);

<NumberTicker value={n} format={{ maximumFractionDigits: 0 }} className="text-title-lg" />
<Button size="sm" variant="outlined" onClick={() => setN(Math.round(Math.random() * 100000))}>
  Change
</Button>
```

## Example: Amount

`Amount animate` uses the ticker and keeps the quieter symbol and minor units.

```tsx
<Amount value={balance} currency="USD" size="display" animate />
```

## Accessibility

- The full value is read as one string; the rolling digits are hidden from assistive tech.
- Under reduced motion digits change instantly.

Related: [amount](amount.md), [stat-card](stat-card.md)

# Pagination

Page navigation control with prev/next and page number buttons.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Navigation · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Pagination } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/pagination

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (required) | `number` |  | The currently active page (1-indexed). |
| `totalItems` (required) | `number` |  | Total number of items across all pages. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | Number of items per page. Used to calculate total page count. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | Number of page buttons to show on each side of the current page. |
| `onPageChange` (required) | `(page: number) => void` |  | Callback invoked with the new page number when the user navigates. |
| `showFirstLast` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to show First and Last page navigation buttons. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables all pagination controls. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
function DefaultPagination() {
  const [page, setPage] = React.useState(3);
  return (
    <Pagination
      page={page}
      totalItems={100}
      pageSize={10}
      onPageChange={setPage}
    />
  );
}
```

## Example: Large dataset

```tsx
function LargeDatasetPagination() {
  const [page, setPage] = React.useState(5);
  return (
    <Pagination
      page={page}
      totalItems={500}
      pageSize={20}
      siblingCount={2}
      onPageChange={setPage}
    />
  );
}
```

# Popover

Floating content panel anchored to a trigger element.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Overlays · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Popover } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/popover

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Popover.Root` | `compound` |  | Root provider that manages open/close state. |
| `Popover.Trigger` | `compound` |  | Element that toggles the popover on click. |
| `Popover.Content` | `compound` |  | The floating content panel. |
| `Popover.Arrow` | `compound` |  | Optional arrow pointing to the trigger. |
| `Popover.Close` | `compound` |  | Button that closes the popover. |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` |  | Preferred side of the trigger to render the content. |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` |  | Alignment of the content relative to the trigger. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` |  | Distance in pixels between the trigger and the content. |
| `surface` | `'solid' \| 'glass'` | `'solid'` | Glass material on Popover.Content — see Foundations → Materials. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Open popover</Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content>
    <Text size="body-sm">Popover content goes here.</Text>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover.Root>
```

## Example: With close button

```tsx
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Settings</Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content side="bottom" align="end" sideOffset={8}>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '8px' }}>
      <Text weight="semibold">Preferences</Text>
      <Text size="body-sm" tone="secondary">Adjust your display settings.</Text>
      <Popover.Close asChild>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Close</Button>
      </Popover.Close>
    </div>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover.Root>
```

# Prompt Input

The composer for a chat: an auto-growing text field with Send, which turns into Stop while a reply streams.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: AI · Status: beta
- Import: `import { PromptInput } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/prompt-input

## When to use

- The message box of a chat or assistant.
- Any free-text prompt that starts a long-running, stoppable generation.

## When not to use

- Ordinary forms: use Textarea, where Enter adds a line.
- Search: use SearchInput.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value / defaultValue / onValueChange` | `string` |  | Controlled or uncontrolled text. Uncontrolled input clears itself after a submit. |
| `onSubmit` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the text on Enter or Send. Not called while empty, disabled or not `idle`. |
| `onStop` | `() => void` |  | Called by Stop, or Escape in the field, while `status="streaming"`. |
| `status` | `'idle' \| 'submitting' \| 'streaming'` | `'idle'` | `streaming` swaps Send for Stop; `submitting` holds Send until the request is accepted. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `8` | Rows the field grows to before it scrolls. |
| `attachments` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered above the text, e.g. removable Chips. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered bottom-start, e.g. an attach IconButton or a model picker. |
| `surface` | `'solid' \| 'glass'` | `'solid'` | Glass material for composers floating over content. |
| `label` | `string` | `messages.promptLabel ('Message')` | Accessible name of the text field. |
| `messages` | `Partial<PromptInputMessages>` |  | Local overrides for `promptLabel`, `sendMessage`, `stopGenerating`, `promptHint`. |
| `textareaClassName` | `string` |  | Class for the textarea; `className` goes to the outer container. |

## Example: Default

Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line. Send stays inert until there is text.

```tsx
<PromptInput placeholder="Ask anything" onSubmit={(text) => send(text)} />
```

## Example: Attachments and actions

```tsx
<PromptInput
  placeholder="Ask about these files"
  attachments={
    <>
      <Chip onRemove={() => remove('q3-report.pdf')}>q3-report.pdf</Chip>
      <Chip onRemove={() => remove('pricing.csv')}>pricing.csv</Chip>
    </>
  }
  actions={
    <>
      <IconButton size="sm" label="Attach files"><Paperclip /></IconButton>
      <IconButton size="sm" label="Search the web"><Globe /></IconButton>
    </>
  }
/>
```

## Example: Streaming

Send a message: the button turns into Stop for three seconds. Stop or Escape ends it early.

```tsx
const [status, setStatus] = React.useState<PromptInputStatus>('idle');
const timer = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>();

function send() {
  setStatus('streaming');
  timer.current = setTimeout(() => setStatus('idle'), 3000);
}

function stop() {
  clearTimeout(timer.current);
  setStatus('idle');
}

<PromptInput placeholder="Ask anything" status={status} onSubmit={send} onStop={stop} />
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: textbox (multiline), button (Send / Stop)
- `Enter`: Sends. Ignored while an IME composition is open.
- `Shift + Enter`: New line.
- `Escape`: Stops the reply while streaming.
- Focus stays in the field after sending, so the user can type the next message straight away.
- An empty field keeps Send focusable with `aria-disabled`, rather than removing it from the tab order.
- The field is named by `label` (default "Message") and described by the Enter/Shift+Enter hint.
- Send and Stop are icon buttons with their own names; the swap does not move focus.

Related: [message-bubble](message-bubble.md), [conversation](conversation.md), [textarea](textarea.md)


---

# Radio Card

A radio group where each option is a whole card: title, description and optional icon, one choice.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Form Controls · Status: beta
- Import: `import { RadioCard } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/radio-card

## When to use

- Two to six options that each need a sentence of explanation, like plans or regions.
- A choice important enough to deserve the space.

## When not to use

- Short labels with no description: use RadioGroup.
- More than six options: use Select or Combobox.
- Cards that hold links or buttons: the whole card is the control, so use Card with CardLink.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RadioCardGroup columns` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `1` | Grid columns. Collapses to one column on narrow screens. |
| `RadioCardGroup value / defaultValue / onValueChange` | `string` |  | Radix RadioGroup props; the group also takes `disabled`, `name`, `required`. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | The option this card selects. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The card’s accessible name. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Secondary text, exposed as the accessible description. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Leading icon. Turns primary when selected. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content under the description. Keep it non-interactive: the whole card is the control. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables this card only. |

## Example: Plan picker

```tsx
const [plan, setPlan] = React.useState('team');

<RadioCardGroup aria-label="Plan" columns={3} value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <RadioCard value="solo" icon={<User />} title="Solo" description="One seat, core features.">
    <span className="text-sm font-medium">$0 / month</span>
  </RadioCard>
  <RadioCard value="team" icon={<Users />} title="Team" description="Up to 20 seats, shared workspaces.">
    <span className="text-sm font-medium">$12 / seat</span>
  </RadioCard>
  <RadioCard value="enterprise" icon={<Building2 />} title="Enterprise" description="SSO, audit logs, priority support.">
    <span className="text-sm font-medium">Contact sales</span>
  </RadioCard>
</RadioCardGroup>
```

## Example: Columns

Two columns from the sm breakpoint up, one below.

```tsx
<RadioCardGroup aria-label="Billing" columns={2} defaultValue="yearly">
  <RadioCard value="monthly" title="Monthly" description="Billed every month." />
  <RadioCard value="yearly" title="Yearly" description="Two months free." />
</RadioCardGroup>
```

## Example: Disabled

Disable one card, or pass `disabled` to the group to disable all of them.

```tsx
<RadioCardGroup aria-label="Region" columns={2} defaultValue="eu">
  <RadioCard value="eu" title="Europe" description="Frankfurt" />
  <RadioCard value="us" title="United States" description="Virginia" />
  <RadioCard value="ap" title="Asia Pacific" description="Coming soon" disabled />
</RadioCardGroup>
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: radiogroup, radio (each card)
- `Tab`: Moves focus into the group, to the selected card.
- `Arrow keys`: Move between cards and select.
- `Space`: Selects the focused card.
- The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description.
- Give the group an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

Related: [radio-group](radio-group.md), [checkbox-card](checkbox-card.md), [card](card.md)


---

# Radio Group

Group of mutually exclusive radio inputs.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Form Controls · Status: stable
- Import: `import { RadioGroup } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/radio-group

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RadioGroup.Root` | `compound` |  | Root provider that manages selection state. |
| `RadioGroup.Item` | `compound` |  | Individual radio option within the group. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The controlled selected value. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The initial selected value when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Callback fired when the selection changes. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables all items in the group. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` |  | Layout orientation of the radio items. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<RadioGroup.Root defaultValue="option-2">
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '8px' }}>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: '8px' }}>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="option-1" id="r1" />
      <Label htmlFor="r1">Option one</Label>
    </div>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: '8px' }}>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="option-2" id="r2" />
      <Label htmlFor="r2">Option two</Label>
    </div>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: '8px' }}>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="option-3" id="r3" />
      <Label htmlFor="r3">Option three</Label>
    </div>
  </div>
</RadioGroup.Root>
```

## Example: Horizontal

```tsx
<RadioGroup.Root defaultValue="monthly" orientation="horizontal">
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '16px' }}>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: '8px' }}>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly" id="monthly" />
      <Label htmlFor="monthly">Monthly</Label>
    </div>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: '8px' }}>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="annual" id="annual" />
      <Label htmlFor="annual">Annual</Label>
    </div>
  </div>
</RadioGroup.Root>
```

# Scroll Area

Scrollable container with custom styled scrollbars.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Disclosure · Status: stable
- Import: `import { ScrollArea } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/scroll-area

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'auto' \| 'always' \| 'scroll' \| 'hover'` | `'hover'` | Controls when the scrollbar is visible. "hover" shows it on mouse-over, "scroll" while scrolling, "always" always, "auto" when content overflows. |
| `scrollHideDelay` | `number` | `600` | Milliseconds before the scrollbar hides after the user stops interacting (only applies to types "scroll" and "hover"). |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | Which axis(es) to make scrollable. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Additional CSS class names applied to the viewport wrapper. |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  | Inline styles applied to the viewport wrapper. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<ScrollArea style={{ height: '200px', width: '280px', border: '1px solid var(--color-border-default)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)', padding: '12px' }}>
  {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => (
    <div key={i} style={{ padding: '4px 0', fontSize: '0.875rem', color: 'var(--color-text-secondary)' }}>
      Item {i + 1}
    </div>
  ))}
</ScrollArea>
```

## Example: Horizontal

```tsx
<ScrollArea orientation="horizontal" style={{ width: '320px', border: '1px solid var(--color-border-default)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)', padding: '12px' }}>
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '8px', width: 'max-content' }}>
    {Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => (
      <div
        key={i}
        style={{
          width: '80px',
          height: '80px',
          background: 'var(--color-bg-subtle)',
          borderRadius: 'var(--radius-sm)',
          display: 'flex',
          alignItems: 'center',
          justifyContent: 'center',
          fontSize: '0.75rem',
          color: 'var(--color-text-secondary)',
          flexShrink: 0,
        }}
      >
        Card {i + 1}
      </div>
    ))}
  </div>
</ScrollArea>
```

# Select

Accessible dropdown select built on Radix UI. Supports groups and search.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Form Controls · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Select } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/select

## When to use

- Choosing a single option from a list of 5+ items
- When screen space is limited and a dropdown collapses the options
- Selecting a region, country, currency, or other enumerated value
- Filtering or configuring a setting with predefined choices

## When not to use

- Fewer than 5 options — use RadioGroup to keep choices visible
- Searching or typing to find an option — use Combobox instead
- Multi-select — use Combobox or a checkbox list
- Boolean on/off choices — use Switch or Checkbox

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | Controlled selected value. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Callback when value changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Placeholder when no value selected. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the select. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Select.Root>
  <Select.Trigger placeholder="Pick a fruit" />
  <Select.Content>
    <Select.Item value="apple">Apple</Select.Item>
    <Select.Item value="banana">Banana</Select.Item>
    <Select.Item value="cherry">Cherry</Select.Item>
  </Select.Content>
</Select.Root>
```

# Sheet

Alias for Drawer — slide-in sheet panel.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Overlays · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Sheet } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/sheet

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Sheet.Root` | `compound` |  | Root provider that manages open/close state. Exported from Drawer. |
| `Sheet.Trigger` | `compound` |  | Element that opens the sheet. |
| `Sheet.Portal` | `compound` |  | Portals the overlay and content into the document body. |
| `Sheet.Overlay` | `compound` |  | Dimmed backdrop rendered behind the sheet. |
| `Sheet.Content` | `compound` |  | The sheet panel. Accepts a side prop. |
| `scrollLock` | `'style' \| 'class'` |  | On Sheet.Root. How page scroll is locked while open. `class` adds a class from @nexub/themes/base instead of injecting a <style> tag, so it works under a strict CSP (style-src 'self'). Default `style`. |
| `side` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom'` |  | Edge of the screen from which the sheet slides in. |
| `Sheet.Header` | `compound` |  | Header section of the sheet panel. |
| `Sheet.Footer` | `compound` |  | Footer section of the sheet panel. |
| `Sheet.Title` | `compound` |  | Accessible title for the sheet. |
| `Sheet.Description` | `compound` |  | Supporting description text for the sheet. |
| `Sheet.Close` | `compound` |  | Element that closes the sheet. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Sheet.Root>
  <Sheet.Trigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Open sheet</Button>
  </Sheet.Trigger>
  <Sheet.Portal>
    <Sheet.Overlay />
    <Sheet.Content side="right">
      <Sheet.Header>
        <Sheet.Title>Notifications</Sheet.Title>
        <Sheet.Description>Review your latest activity.</Sheet.Description>
      </Sheet.Header>
      <div style={{ padding: '16px', flex: 1 }}>
        <Text size="body-sm" tone="secondary">No new notifications.</Text>
      </div>
      <Sheet.Footer>
        <Sheet.Close asChild>
          <Button variant="outline">Close</Button>
        </Sheet.Close>
      </Sheet.Footer>
    </Sheet.Content>
  </Sheet.Portal>
</Sheet.Root>
```

# Split Button

A primary action with related secondary actions behind a chevron, as one connected control.

```tsx
</SplitButton>
```

# Streaming Text

Assistant text as it arrives: new chunks fade in, text already shown stays still, and a caret marks the end.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: AI · Status: beta
- Import: `import { StreamingText } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/streaming-text

## When to use

- Any model output rendered token by token.

## When not to use

- Finished text loaded from history: render it as plain text, or with `streaming={false}`.
- Model output as HTML or Markdown HTML: StreamingText renders text only. Parse Markdown to React elements yourself; never inject model HTML.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (required) | `string` |  | The full text received so far. Append to it; anything that is not an append renders statically. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the caret and sets `aria-busy` while more text is expected. |
| `as` | `'div' \| 'p' \| 'span'` | `'div'` | Element to render. |
| `aria-live` | `'off' \| 'polite'` | `'off'` | Opt-in live announcements. Leave off: screen readers would re-read the region on every token. |

## Example: Streaming a reply

Words arrive on a timer. Restart streams the paragraph again.

```tsx
const reply = 'Tokens arrive a few characters at a time. Each new chunk fades in while the text before it stays put, so the eye can keep reading.';
const [length, setLength] = React.useState(0);
const streaming = length < reply.length;

React.useEffect(() => {
  if (!streaming) return;
  const id = setTimeout(() => setLength((n) => Math.min(reply.length, n + 6)), 60);
  return () => clearTimeout(id);
}, [length, streaming]);

<StreamingText as="p" text={reply.slice(0, length)} streaming={streaming} />
<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setLength(0)}>Restart</Button>
```

## Accessibility

- Not a live region by default. Announce the finished message once instead, e.g. through a polite status or Conversation’s `announce` for whole messages.
- `aria-busy` is true while streaming, so assistive tech can wait for the final text.
- The caret is decorative (`aria-hidden`). With reduced motion, chunks appear without fading and the caret does not blink.
- Only the last three chunks keep their own span, so the DOM stays flat however long the reply gets.

Related: [message-bubble](message-bubble.md), [thinking-indicator](thinking-indicator.md), [conversation](conversation.md)

# Table

Semantic HTML table with styled variants.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Data Display · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Table } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/table

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Table.Root striped` | `boolean` | `false` | Applies alternating row background colours. |
| `Table.Root bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds borders between rows and columns. |
| `Table.Root hoverable` | `boolean` | `false` | Highlights rows on mouse hover. |
| `Table.Root stickyHeader` | `boolean` | `false` | Fixes the table header to the top when scrolling inside a scrollable container. |
| `Table.Head align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'start'` | Text alignment within the header cell. |
| `Table.Cell align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'start'` | Text alignment within the data cell. |
| `Table.Caption side` | `'top' \| 'bottom'` | `'bottom'` | Whether the caption appears above or below the table. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Table.Root>
  <Table.Header>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Head>Name</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head>Status</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head>Date</Table.Head>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Header>
  <Table.Body>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell>Alice Johnson</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell><StatusPill tone="success" label="Active" /></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>12 Jan 2026</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell>Bob Martinez</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell><StatusPill tone="warning" label="Pending" /></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>18 Feb 2026</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell>Carol Smith</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell><StatusPill tone="neutral" label="Inactive" /></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>03 Mar 2026</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Body>
</Table.Root>
```

## Example: With caption

```tsx
<Table.Root>
  <Table.Caption>Recent user activity — last 30 days</Table.Caption>
  <Table.Header>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Head>Name</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head>Status</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head>Date</Table.Head>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Header>
  <Table.Body>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell>Alice Johnson</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell><StatusPill tone="success" label="Active" /></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>12 Jan 2026</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell>Bob Martinez</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell><StatusPill tone="warning" label="Pending" /></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>18 Feb 2026</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell>Carol Smith</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell><StatusPill tone="neutral" label="Inactive" /></Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>03 Mar 2026</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Body>
  <Table.Footer>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell colSpan={3} style={{ color: 'var(--color-text-secondary)', fontSize: '0.875rem' }}>
        Showing 3 of 3 users
      </Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Footer>
</Table.Root>
```

# Tabs

Layered content panels switched by tab triggers. Built on Radix UI Tabs.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Navigation · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Tabs } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/tabs

## When to use

- Switching between related views within the same page context
- Organising content that belongs to the same entity
- Reducing visual clutter by hiding secondary content behind tabs
- Horizontal navigation within a bounded section

## When not to use

- Global site navigation — use the sidebar or top nav
- Sequential steps in order — use StepIndicator
- Comparing content side-by-side — keep both views visible
- More than 5–7 tabs — consider a Select or sub-navigation

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | Initially active tab value (uncontrolled). |
| `value` | `string` |  | Controlled active tab value. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Callback when active tab changes. |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Layout direction of the tab list. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<Tabs.Root defaultValue="account">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="account">Account</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="billing">Billing</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="notifications">Notifications</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Content value="account">
    <Text>Account settings content.</Text>
  </Tabs.Content>
  <Tabs.Content value="billing">
    <Text>Billing details content.</Text>
  </Tabs.Content>
  <Tabs.Content value="notifications">
    <Text>Notification preferences content.</Text>
  </Tabs.Content>
</Tabs.Root>
```

# Tag

> **Deprecated.** Do not use in new code. Deprecated — use Badge. Non-interactive label tag for categorisation.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Labels & Badges · Status: deprecated
- Import: `import { Tag } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/tag

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'solid' \| 'soft' \| 'outline'` | `'soft'` | Visual style of the tag. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | Semantic colour tone of the tag. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Controls tag size. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '8px' }}>
  <Tag>Frontend</Tag>
  <Tag tone="info">Backend</Tag>
  <Tag tone="success">Deployed</Tag>
</div>
```

# Text

Paragraph text component with size, tone, and weight variants.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Typography · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Text } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/text

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'body-lg' \| 'body' \| 'body-sm' \| 'caption' \| 'label'` | `'body'` | Controls the font size and line height. |
| `tone` | `'default' \| 'secondary' \| 'muted' \| 'subtle' \| 'inverse'` |  | Color tone applied to the text. |
| `weight` | `'regular' \| 'medium' \| 'semibold' \| 'bold'` |  | Font weight of the text. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` |  | Truncates text with an ellipsis when it overflows. |
| `lineClamp` | `number` |  | Clamps the text to a maximum number of lines. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Merges props onto the immediate child element (Radix Slot). |

## Example: Default

```tsx

```

## Example: Sizes

```tsx

  <Text size="body">Body — the default reading size.</Text>
  <Text size="body-sm">Body small — secondary content and descriptions.</Text>
  <Text size="caption">Caption — metadata and timestamps.</Text>
</div>
```

## Example: Tones

```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '8px' }}>
  <Text tone="default">Default tone</Text>
  <Text tone="secondary">Secondary tone</Text>

</div>
```

# Thinking Indicator

Shows the assistant is working before the first token arrives: a morphing shape and a shimmering label.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: AI · Status: beta
- Import: `import { ThinkingIndicator } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/thinking-indicator

## When to use

- The gap between sending a prompt and the first token of the reply.
- Tool calls or retrieval steps inside a reply, with a label naming the step.

## When not to use

- Once text is streaming: StreamingText’s caret already shows progress. Replace the indicator, don’t stack them.
- General loading outside AI surfaces: use Spinner or Skeleton.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode \| null` | `messages.thinking ('Thinking')` | Visible text. `null` hides it; "Thinking" is still announced. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Shape and text size. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ thinking: string }>` |  | Local override for the default text. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<ThinkingIndicator />
```

## Example: Custom label and sizes

Name the step when you know it. `label={null}` keeps only the shape.

```tsx
<ThinkingIndicator label="Searching 4 sources" />
<ThinkingIndicator size="sm" />
<ThinkingIndicator size="sm" label={null} />
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: status
- A polite live region: the label is announced once when it mounts. Changing the label announces the new step.
- Render it only while waiting and remove it when tokens start, so it is not announced again.
- With reduced motion the shape and shimmer are static.

Related: [streaming-text](streaming-text.md), [spinner](spinner.md), [conversation](conversation.md)

# Toast

Imperative toast notifications using the toast object. Render <Toaster /> once in your layout.

- Package: `@nexub/react` · Category: Feedback · Status: stable
- Import: `import { Toast } from '@nexub/react';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/components/toast

## When to use

- Confirming a non-blocking action (file saved, message sent)
- Reporting a background event the user should know about
- Providing brief feedback that disappears automatically
- Offering an undo action immediately after a destructive operation

## When not to use

- Critical errors that block the user — use Alert or AlertDialog
- Information the user must read and acknowledge — use Dialog
- Persistent status that should remain visible — use Banner or Alert
- Long messages with multiple lines of text

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Toaster expand` | `boolean` | `false` | Always show toasts as a list. By default they collapse into a stack that fans out on hover or focus, which also pauses their timers. |
| `Toaster visibleToasts` | `number` | `3` | How many toasts show at once. Older ones are hidden visually but stay in the live region. |
| `toast.success(title, opts?)` (required) | `string` |  | Show a success toast with an optional options object. |
| `toast.error(title, opts?)` (required) | `string` |  | Show an error toast. |
| `toast.warning(title, opts?)` (required) | `string` |  | Show a warning toast. |
| `toast.info(title, opts?)` (required) | `string` |  | Show an info toast. |
| `toast.custom(title, opts?)` (required) | `string` |  | Show a default/custom toast. |
| `toast.undoable(title, opts)` (required) | `UndoableToastOptions` |  | A toast with an Undo action (beta, 1.7.0). Undo calls `opts.onUndo`; any other close (timer, swipe, close button, `toast.dismiss`) calls `opts.onCommit`, exactly once. Returns the toast id. |
| `undoable opts` | `{ onUndo; onCommit?; undoLabel?; description?; duration? }` |  | `undoLabel` defaults to the `undo` message ("Undo"). Commit the change in `onCommit`, not before showing the toast. |
| `opts.description` | `string` |  | Secondary supporting text below the title. |
| `opts.duration` | `number` | `5000` | Time in ms before auto-dismiss. Use Infinity to persist. |
| `opts.action` | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | Renders an action button inside the toast. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
function DefaultToast() {
  return (
    <>
      <Toaster />
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() => toast.custom('Changes saved', { description: 'Your profile has been updated.' })}
      >
        Show toast
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Example: Variants

```tsx
function ToastVariants() {
  return (
    <>
      <Toaster />
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '8px', flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.custom('Default notification')}>
          Default
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.success('Saved successfully')}>
          Success
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.error('Something went wrong')}>
          Error
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.warning('Proceed with caution')}>
          Warning
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.info('New update available')}>
          Info
        </Button>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Example: With action

```tsx
function ToastWithAction() {
  return (
    <>
      <Toaster />
      <Button
        variant="outline"
        onClick={() =>
          toast.custom('Message sent', {
            description: 'Your message has been delivered to the team.',
            action: {
              label: 'Undo',
              onClick: () => {},
            },
          })
        }
      >
        Send message
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Example: Undoable delete

Hide the item right away; delete it for real only when the toast closes without Undo.

```tsx
function UndoableDelete() {
  const [hidden, setHidden] = React.useState(false);

  function remove() {
    setHidden(true);
    toast.undoable('Invoice deleted', {
      description: 'INV-2041',
      onUndo: () => setHidden(false),
      onCommit: () => deleteInvoice('INV-2041'),
    });
  }

  return (
    <>
      <Toaster />
      {hidden ? (
        <Button variant="text" onClick={() => setHidden(false)}>Restore demo</Button>
      ) : (
        <Button variant="outline" tone="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete INV-2041</Button>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

# Bento Grid

A grid of card tiles in mixed sizes. Responds to its own width: 1 column, 2 at 480px, 4 at 768px.

- Package: `@nexub/patterns` · Category: Layout · Status: beta
- Import: `import { BentoGrid } from '@nexub/patterns';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/patterns/bento-grid

## When to use

- Overview pages where a few items deserve more room than the rest.

## When not to use

- Lists the user scans in order: dense packing can move tiles out of reading order.
- Equal-weight items: use Grid.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BentoGrid children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | `BentoTile`s. Dense packing back-fills gaps left by large tiles, so visual order can differ from source order. |
| `size` | `'1x1' \| '2x1' \| '1x2' \| '2x2'` | `'1x1'` | Tile span, columns × rows. Two-wide spans apply from 2 columns up. |
| `...Card props` | `CardProps` |  | A tile is a surface Card (`variant` is fixed); `tone`, `surface` and `effect` pass through. |

## Example: Dashboard

```tsx
<BentoGrid>
  <BentoTile size="2x2">
    <h3 className="text-title-sm">Revenue, last 7 days</h3>
    <RevenueChart />
  </BentoTile>
  <BentoTile><StatTile label="Active users" value="12,480" /></BentoTile>
  <BentoTile><StatTile label="Conversion" value="3.2%" /></BentoTile>
  <BentoTile size="2x1">3 invoices awaiting approval.</BentoTile>
  <BentoTile><StatTile label="Churn" value="0.8%" /></BentoTile>
  <BentoTile><StatTile label="NPS" value="61" /></BentoTile>
</BentoGrid>
```

Related: [card](card.md), [stat-card](stat-card.md)

# Conversation

Chat layout: a scrolling message list that follows new content, with a sticky composer underneath.

- Package: `@nexub/patterns` · Category: AI · Status: beta
- Import: `import { Conversation } from '@nexub/patterns';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/patterns/conversation

## When to use

- A full chat or assistant view: messages above, composer below.

## When not to use

- A single question and answer: a PromptInput and a MessageBubble in normal flow are enough.
- Comment threads that don’t follow new content: use ActivityFeed.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The messages, usually MessageBubbles. |
| `composer` | `ReactNode` |  | Sticky slot under the list, usually a PromptInput. |
| `autoScroll` | `boolean` | `true` | Follow new content while the reader is at the bottom. Scrolling up stops following and shows "Jump to latest". |
| `announce` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the list a polite `role="log"`. Only for whole-message updates: with token streaming it announces every chunk. |
| `messages` | `Partial<ConversationMessages>` |  | Overrides for `jumpToLatest` and `conversation`. |

## Example: Mini chat

Send a message: it shows Thinking, then streams a cited reply. Stop or Escape ends the reply early.

```tsx
type Message = { id: number; from: 'user' | 'assistant'; text: string };

const REPLY = 'Air-source heat pumps work in most homes and run at roughly the cost of gas.';
const SOURCE = { title: 'Choosing a heat pump', url: 'https://example.com/guides/heat-pumps' };

function Chat() {
  const [messages, setMessages] = React.useState<Message[]>([]);
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState<'idle' | 'submitting' | 'streaming'>('idle');
  const timer = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>();

  function send(text: string) {
    const id = Date.now();
    setMessages((m) => [...m, { id, from: 'user', text }, { id: id + 1, from: 'assistant', text: '' }]);
    setStatus('submitting');
    timer.current = setTimeout(() => {
      setStatus('streaming');
      stream(id + 1, 0);
    }, 800);
  }

  function stream(id: number, length: number) {
    setMessages((m) => m.map((msg) => (msg.id === id ? { ...msg, text: REPLY.slice(0, length) } : msg)));
    if (length >= REPLY.length) return setStatus('idle');
    timer.current = setTimeout(() => stream(id, length + 4), 50);
  }

  function stop() {
    clearTimeout(timer.current);
    setStatus('idle');
  }

  const last = messages[messages.length - 1];

  return (
    <Conversation
      style={{ height: 420 }}
      composer={<PromptInput placeholder="Ask about heat pumps" status={status} onSubmit={send} onStop={stop} />}
    >
      {messages.map((msg) =>
        msg.from === 'user' ? (
          <MessageBubble key={msg.id} from="user">{msg.text}</MessageBubble>
        ) : (
          <MessageBubble key={msg.id} from="assistant">
            {status === 'submitting' && msg === last ? (
              <ThinkingIndicator />
            ) : (
              <>
                <StreamingText as="span" text={msg.text} streaming={status === 'streaming' && msg === last} />
                {msg.text === REPLY && <Citation index={1} source={SOURCE} />}
              </>
            )}
          </MessageBubble>
        ),
      )}
    </Conversation>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: region (default) or log (with `announce`)
- `Tab`: The message list is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
- Keep focus in the composer while a reply streams; don’t move it to the new message.
- The list is named "Conversation". Leave `announce` off while streaming tokens and announce the finished reply once instead.
- With reduced motion, "Jump to latest" scrolls instantly.

Related: [message-bubble](message-bubble.md), [prompt-input](prompt-input.md), [streaming-text](streaming-text.md)


---

# Error Summary

Lists a form’s errors after a failed submit, with a link to each field. useFormErrors wires the fields to their messages.

- Package: `@nexub/patterns` · Category: Forms · Status: beta
- Import: `import { ErrorSummary } from '@nexub/patterns';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/patterns/error-summary

## When to use

- Forms validated on submit, especially long ones where some errors are off screen.
- Alongside inline messages, never instead of them.

## When not to use

- Live validation while typing: pass a new array per submit, not per keystroke, or the summary steals focus.
- A single field: the inline message is enough.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` (required) | `{ id: string; message: string }[]` |  | One entry per invalid field; `id` is the field’s DOM id. Renders nothing when empty. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `'There is a problem'` | Heading; it also labels the summary. |
| `onFocusField` | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called after a link moves focus to its field. |
| `useFormErrors(map)` (required) | `Record<string, string \| null \| undefined \| false>` |  | Takes `{ fieldId: message }`. Falsy messages are skipped. |
| `→ errors` | `ErrorSummaryItem[]` |  | The list for `ErrorSummary`. Stable for the same map object. |
| `→ fieldProps(id)` | `function` |  | Spread on the input: `id`, plus `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby="${id}-error"` when it has an error. |
| `→ errorProps(id)` | `function` |  | Spread on the inline message: `id="${id}-error"`, the same id FormField.Error uses. |

## Example: Validate on submit

Submit empty to see the summary. A new map per submit moves focus to the summary; links jump to each field.

```tsx
function SignUp() {
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = React.useState<FormErrorMap>({});
  const { errors, fieldProps, errorProps } = useFormErrors(submitted);

  function submit(e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    const data = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
    setSubmitted({
      name: String(data.get('name')).trim() ? undefined : 'Enter your name',
      email: /^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/.test(String(data.get('email'))) ? undefined : 'Enter an email address, like name@example.com',
    });
  }

  return (
    <form noValidate onSubmit={submit}>
      <ErrorSummary errors={errors} />
      <Label htmlFor="name">Name</Label>
      <Input name="name" {...fieldProps('name')} invalid={Boolean(submitted.name)} />
      {submitted.name && <FormError {...errorProps('name')}>{submitted.name}</FormError>}
      <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
      <Input name="email" type="email" {...fieldProps('email')} invalid={Boolean(submitted.email)} />
      {submitted.email && <FormError {...errorProps('email')}>{submitted.email}</FormError>}
      <Button type="submit">Create account</Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

- Roles: alert
- Takes focus whenever it receives a new, non-empty `errors` array, so screen readers read it and keyboard users start from it.
- Each link scrolls its field into view and focuses it.
- An `alert` labelled by its heading. Fields get `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` pointing at their inline message.

Related: [form-field](form-field.md), [input](input.md), [alert](alert.md)

# FilterBar

Search + filter toolbar pattern for data-heavy list or table views.

- Package: `@nexub/patterns` · Category: Data · Status: stable
- Import: `import { FilterBar } from '@nexub/patterns';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/patterns/filter-bar

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `'Search…'` | Placeholder text for the search input. |
| `searchValue` | `string` |  | Controlled search value. |
| `onSearch` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Callback when search value changes. |
| `filters` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Filter controls rendered to the right of search. |
| `actions` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Action buttons (e.g. "Export") rendered on the far right. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<FilterBar
  searchPlaceholder="Search users…"
  onSearch={(v) => {}}
  filters={
    <Select.Root>
      <Select.Trigger><Select.Value placeholder="Status" /></Select.Trigger>
      <Select.Content>
        <Select.Item value="active">Active</Select.Item>
        <Select.Item value="inactive">Inactive</Select.Item>
      </Select.Content>
    </Select.Root>
  }
  actions={<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Export</Button>}
/>
```

# List Detail

The list-detail layout: side by side at 720px+ of its own width (a container query), one pane at a time below.

- Package: `@nexub/patterns` · Category: Layout · Status: beta
- Import: `import { ListDetail } from '@nexub/patterns';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/patterns/list-detail

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list / detail` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The two panes. |
| `showDetail` | `boolean` | `false` | When narrow, show the detail instead of the list (set it on selection). |
| `onBack` | `() => void` |  | Back button, shown only when narrow. |
| `listWidth` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Fixed list width when both panes show (288 / 320 / 400px). |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<ListDetail
  showDetail={selected !== null}
  onBack={() => setSelected(null)}
  list={<MessageList onSelect={setSelected} />}
  detail={<Message id={selected} />}
/>
```

# StatCard

Metric display card showing a KPI value, label, optional delta, and icon.

- Package: `@nexub/patterns` · Category: Data · Status: stable
- Import: `import { StatCard } from '@nexub/patterns';`
- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/patterns/stat-card

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Metric name label. |
| `value` (required) | `React.ReactNode` |  | Primary metric value. |
| `delta` | `string` |  | Change value (e.g. "+12.5%"). |
| `deltaType` | `'increase' \| 'decrease' \| 'neutral'` |  | Semantic direction of the delta. |
| `sentiment` | `'positive' \| 'negative' \| 'neutral'` |  | Colour of the delta, independent of the arrow. Defaults from `deltaType`; use it when a decrease is good news (e.g. churn down). |
| `icon` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Icon displayed in the card header. |
| `description` | `string` |  | Additional context below the value. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `false` | Roll the digits when a number or string `value` changes (NumberTicker), announced politely. The first render never animates. |

## Example: Default

```tsx
<StatCard
  label="Total Revenue"
  value="$48,295"
  delta="+12.5%"
  deltaType="increase"
  description="vs last month"
/>
```

## Example: With icon

```tsx
<StatCard
  label="Active Users"
  value="2,841"
  delta="-3.2%"
  deltaType="decrease"
  icon={<Users size={20} />}
/>
```

## Example: Animated

```tsx
<StatCard label="Orders today" value={orders.toLocaleString()} animate />
```

# @nexub/react-native

React Native components and screen patterns for Nexub Design System. They use the same tokens, brands and prop names as `@nexub/react` on the web.

**Native chrome, Nexub content.** The system draws the tab bar, stack header, back gesture, action sheets, pickers and iOS 26 Liquid Glass; Nexub themes them. Everything inside a screen (lists, cards, buttons, inputs, money) is drawn by Nexub, so it looks the same on iOS, Android and the web.

Status: **alpha**. Built for Expo SDK 57+ / React Native 0.86+ (New Architecture). Works in Expo apps and bare React Native apps.

## Install

```bash
npx expo install @nexub/react-native react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-svg react-native-safe-area-context expo-font
```

Optional peers. Add only what you use; without them the feature is a no-op or the component tells you what to install:

| Package | Used by |
|---|---|
| `expo-haptics` | Semantic haptics on every control |
| `expo-glass-effect` | Native Liquid Glass (`Surface material="glass"`) on iOS 26+ |
| `expo-screen-capture` | `PrivacyShield preventCapture` |
| `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` | `DateTimeField` |

`@nexub/tokens`, `@nexub/core`, `@nexub/icons` and the fonts (Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans, Geist Mono; OFL) come with the package.

## Set up

```tsx
import { useFonts } from 'expo-font';
import { Stack } from 'expo-router';
import { NexubNativeProvider, ToastProvider, nexubFonts, useNexubNavigation } from '@nexub/react-native';

function Screens() {
  const nav = useNexubNavigation(); // native stack in Nexub colours and type
  return <Stack screenOptions={nav.stack} />;
}

export default function RootLayout() {
  const [ready] = useFonts(nexubFonts);
  if (!ready) return null;
  return (
    <NexubNativeProvider product="payub">
      <ToastProvider>
        <Screens />
      </ToastProvider>
    </NexubNativeProvider>
  );
}
```

`NexubNativeProvider` props:

| Prop | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `scheme` | `'system'` | `'light'`, `'dark'` or follow the OS |
| `contrast` | `'system'` | follows iOS Increase Contrast / Android high-contrast text (re-read on foreground) |
| `product` | none | `'leap' \| 'bookub' \| 'payub' \| 'founderub'`: remaps the tertiary family |
| `seed`, `seedTarget` | none | white-label colour: regenerates the primary (or tertiary) family with contrast-safe tones |
| `glass` | `'balanced'` | the user's glass dial; forced `'off'` under Reduce Transparency |
| `haptics` | `true` | the user's haptics setting |
| `fonts` | `'nexub'` | `'system'` to use the platform font |
| `locale`, `dir`, `messages` | `'en'` | Intl locale, RTL (derived from the locale) and translated strings, same as web `NexubProvider` |

Hooks: `useTheme()`, `useRoles()`, `useHaptics()`, `useNexubMessages()`, `useNexubNavigation()`.

## Components

Names and props match `@nexub/react` where a web twin exists.

- **Primitives:** `Text`, `Heading`, `Pressable` (state layer, 0.97 press spring, haptic), `Surface` (tonal tiers, elevation, glass), `Box`, `Stack`, `Inline`, `Icon`, `ScreenContainer`.
- **Actions:** `Button`, `IconButton`, `ButtonGroup`, `Link`.
- **Data:** `Amount`, `Badge`, `Avatar`, `AvatarGroup`, `Divider`.
- **Inputs:** `TextField`, `PasswordInput`, `SearchField`, `MoneyInput`, `Stepper`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup` / `Radio`, `Switch` (the platform switch), `SegmentedControl`, `Slider`, `Chip`, `FilterChip`, `Select`, `DateTimeField`, `OTPInput`, `NumericKeypad`, `ExpressiveMoneyInput`.
- **Containers:** `Card`, `ListItem` (navigation, switch, checkbox, radio, button and value rows), `ListSection`, `Accordion`.
- **Overlays:** `BottomSheet` (detents), `ActionSheet` (system sheet on iOS), `ContextMenu`, `Dialog`.
- **Feedback:** `Banner`, `ToastProvider` / `useToast`, `Progress`, `LoadingIndicator`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `OfflineBanner`, `Coachmark`.
- **Mobile:** `SwipeableRow`, `RefreshControl`, `Carousel`, `PageIndicator`, `StickyFooter`, `SensitiveValue`, `PrivacyShield`, `FAB` (Android only by default).
- **Navigation helpers:** `nexubStackOptions`, `nexubNavigationTheme`, `nexubTabsOptions`.

Icons: `import { Search } from '@nexub/icons/native'`. These are the same names as `@nexub/icons`. Colour them with `<Icon icon={Search} color="primary" />`.

## Patterns

`import { SignInScreen, AmountStep, ActivityList } from '@nexub/react-native/patterns'`. Each pattern is a screen template that takes data and callbacks, so it works with any router.

- **Auth:** `AuthScreen`, `SignInScreen`, `VerifyCodeScreen`, `LockScreen`.
- **Money:** `FlowStep`, `AmountStep`, `ReviewStep`, `ActivityList`, `TransactionDetail`, `ResultScreen`.
- **App:** `OnboardingScreen`, `PermissionPrimer`, `SettingsScreen`, `ProfileHeader`, `AppearanceSection`, `NotificationsInbox`, `SearchScreen`, `ChatScreen`, `PaywallScreen`, `AppSwitcherSheet`.

## Rules the components follow

- **Touch targets:** every control reaches 44pt (`hitSlop` on smaller visuals). Primary actions use `size="lg"` (48).
- **Text scaling:** every role scales with the system text size. iOS follows Apple's Dynamic Type curve per role, and display and headline roles are capped so they don't push content off screen.
- **Screen readers:**
  - A list row is one element ("Amazon, −$42.50, today").
  - Swipe and long-press actions are also accessibility actions.
  - Masked values read as "hidden".
  - Toasts are announced.
- **Haptics are semantic** (`selection`, `toggleOn`/`toggleOff`, `confirm`, `reject`, `warning`, `snap`), never on plain taps, and never the only feedback.
- **Motion:** M3 springs (no overshoot by default), off under Reduce Motion.
- **Glass:** for the control layer only, never content. It is native Liquid Glass on iOS 26+, solid elsewhere and whenever the user turns transparency down.
- **Security:** `OTPInput` uses one field, so SMS autofill works. `PasswordInput` sets the platform autofill hints. `SensitiveValue` re-masks when the app backgrounds. `PrivacyShield` covers the app-switcher snapshot. The library makes no network calls and stores nothing.

## Testing your app

The library's own tests use Jest (jest-expo) and React Native Testing Library. In your Jest setup, stub `react-native-reanimated`'s APIs and use `react-native-safe-area-context/jest/mock`; `packages/react-native/jest.setup.js` in the repo shows the pattern.

## Links

- Docs: https://nexub-ds-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/react-native
- Plan and decisions: [MOBILE_PLAN.md](https://github.com/Nexub-AI/nexub-ds/blob/development/MOBILE_PLAN.md)
- Web components: `@nexub/react`
